coded.vl: The general labor statute applies in full
coded.n: The Labor Standards Act applies to trainees as employees.
coded.src: Technical Intern Training Act 2016

coded.vl: The national statutory minimum wage applies
coded.n: Prefectural minimum wages apply.
coded.src: Minimum Wage Act

coded.vl: Only minimum rest periods apply, or limits apply with sector exclusions
coded.n: Hours, break and rest-day rules apply, except in agriculture, livestock, sericulture and fisheries; forestry is not exempt.
coded.src: Labor Standards Act Art. 41(i) and Appended Table 1 items 6–7

coded.vl: Cannot change without the employer's consent
coded.n: The current Act gives trainees no right to request a change of employer. Under Employment for Skill Development (from 1 April 2027) a worker may request a change in the same field after a period of one to two years set by ordinance, subject to skill and Japanese-language standards, with exceptions for unavoidable circumstances.
coded.src: Technical Intern Training Act (No. 89 of 2016) Art. 19; amending Act No. 60 of 2024, Arts 8-2, 9-2

coded.vl: May form and join unions on equal terms
coded.n: May form and join unions.
coded.src: Trade Union Act

coded.vl: Fees charged to the worker are capped or regulated
coded.n: Bilateral memoranda bind sending states to screen agencies; fees charged in sending countries are not prohibited under Japanese law. The 2027 system is to share costs with employers.
coded.src: Memoranda of cooperation; US TIP Report 2025

coded.vl: Enrolled in the national labor or health insurance schemes
coded.n: Enrolled in employees' health and pension insurance (all legal residents staying over three months must be enrolled). Public schemes leave a copayment of about 30%, and the government recommends supplementary private insurance for trainees.
coded.src: Health Insurance Act; Oishi and Chien (2026)

coded.vl: A dedicated public channel for migrant workers in their languages
coded.n: OTIT consultation in eight languages; labor inspection offices.
coded.src: Organization for Technical Intern Training (official guidance)

coded.vl: May move to another status that can lead to permanent residence, on conditions
coded.n: Maximum five years as a trainee; may move to Specified Skilled Worker, from which (ii) can lead to permanent residence.
coded.src: Immigration Control Act; Immigration Services Agency

coded.vl: Barred
coded.n: Technical intern training is excluded from the statuses whose families may hold Dependent status.
coded.src: Immigration Control Act, Appended Table I(4)

coded.vl: The general labor statute applies in full
coded.n: The Labor Standards Act applies.

coded.vl: The national statutory minimum wage applies
coded.n: Pay must at least equal that of Japanese workers in the same job.

coded.src: Labor Standards Act Art. 41(i) and Appended Table 1 items 6–7

coded.vl: May change employer without the employer's consent
coded.n: May change employer within the same field.
coded.src: Immigration Services Agency

coded.vl: May form and join unions on equal terms
coded.n: May form and join unions.
coded.src: Trade Union Act

coded.vl: Fees charged to the worker are capped or regulated
coded.n: Bilateral memoranda with sending states address fees; not prohibited in Japanese law.
coded.src: Memoranda of cooperation

coded.vl: Enrolled in the national labor or health insurance schemes
coded.n: Enrolled in employees' health insurance and employees' pension from the first day of employment at covered workplaces; the three-month residence rule applies only to National Health Insurance.
coded.src: Health Insurance Act Arts 3, 35; Employees' Pension Insurance Act Art. 9; Oishi and Chien (2026)

coded.vl: A dedicated public channel for migrant workers in their languages
coded.n: Registered support organizations must give consultation in the worker's language.

coded.n: SSW (i) is capped at five years in total, or six with good reason, not counting time lost to pregnancy, childbirth or childcare (from 1 Apr 2026); SSW (ii) has no cap and can lead to permanent residence under the general criteria.

changes.en: Amended Immigration Act allows employers' associations to take in foreign trainees.
Technical Intern Training introduced, together with the Japan International Training Cooperation Organization (month approximate).
Technical Intern Training Act in force; Organization for Technical Intern Training created.
Specified Skilled Worker status introduced, with change of employer allowed within a field.
Diet passes the act replacing Technical Intern Training with Employment for Skill Development (Act No. 60 of 2024, promulgated 21 June).
Employment for Skill Development scheduled to start.

dec.pe: A US English teacher in Japan joined peaceful protests. Japan refused to renew his visa. The Supreme Court said foreigners have constitutional rights, but the government has wide freedom to decide on visas.
dec.pi: Seorang guru bahasa Inggris dari AS di Jepang ikut unjuk rasa damai. Jepang menolak memperpanjang visanya. MA menyatakan orang asing punya hak konstitusional, tetapi pemerintah punya keleluasaan luas atas visa.

dec.n: Local voting rights of permanent residents
dec.pe: Korean permanent residents asked to vote in local elections. The Supreme Court said the Constitution does not give them that right, but Parliament could give it by law.
dec.pi: Penduduk tetap keturunan Korea meminta hak memilih dalam pemilihan daerah. MA menyatakan konstitusi tidak memberi hak itu, tetapi parlemen boleh memberikannya lewat UU.

dec.n: Lost earnings of an injured worker without a visa
dec.pe: A Pakistani worker without a visa was injured in a Japanese factory. The Supreme Court said the employer must pay damages, counting Japanese wages for a limited time and home-country wages after that.
dec.pi: Seorang pekerja Pakistan tanpa visa terluka di pabrik di Jepang. MA menyatakan majikan wajib membayar ganti rugi, menghitung upah Jepang untuk jangka terbatas lalu upah negara asal sesudahnya.

dec.n: Chong Hyang Gyun v. Tokyo Metropolitan Government
dec.pe: A Korean nurse born and working in Japan was not allowed to sit Tokyo’s promotion exam because she was not a citizen. The Supreme Court said this was allowed.
dec.pi: Seorang perawat keturunan Korea yang lahir dan bekerja di Jepang tidak diizinkan mengikuti ujian promosi di Tokyo karena bukan warga negara. MA menyatakan hal itu boleh.

dec.pe: Children of Filipina mothers and Japanese fathers who were not married could not get Japanese nationality. The Supreme Court said this was unequal. The law was changed the same year.
dec.pi: Anak-anak dari ibu Filipina dan ayah Jepang yang tidak menikah tidak bisa mendapat kewarganegaraan Jepang. MA menyatakan ini tidak setara. UU diubah pada tahun yang sama.

dec.pe: An elderly Chinese woman who had lived in Japan for decades was refused welfare. The Supreme Court said foreigners have no legal right to welfare, though the government may give it voluntarily.
dec.pi: Seorang perempuan lanjut usia asal Tiongkok yang tinggal puluhan tahun di Jepang ditolak bantuan sosial. MA menyatakan orang asing tidak punya hak hukum atas bantuan sosial, walau pemerintah boleh memberinya secara sukarela.

dec.n: Deportation right after an asylum refusal (Sri Lankan nationals)
dec.pe: Two Sri Lankan men were told their asylum objection had failed and were put on a plane the next day. The Tokyo High Court said this denied them their right to go to court.
dec.pi: Dua pria Sri Lanka diberi tahu keberatan suaka mereka gagal dan diterbangkan keesokan harinya. Pengadilan Tinggi Tokyo menyatakan ini menghilangkan hak mereka untuk ke pengadilan.

dec.n: Death of a Cameroonian man in immigration detention (Ushiku)
dec.pe: A man from Cameroon died in 2014 in an immigration detention centre in Ushiku after crying out in pain through the night. The court said staff failed to get him to hospital and awarded damages to his family.
dec.pi: Seorang pria dari Kamerun meninggal pada 2014 di pusat detensi imigrasi Ushiku setelah semalaman mengerang kesakitan. Pengadilan menyatakan petugas lalai membawanya ke rumah sakit dan memberi ganti rugi kepada keluarganya.

dec.n: Le Thi Thuy Linh case (technical intern acquitted)
dec.pe: A young Vietnamese woman working on a farm in Japan hid her pregnancy because she feared being sent home. Her twins were stillborn and she was convicted of abandoning their bodies. The Supreme Court acquitted her.
dec.pi: Seorang perempuan muda Vietnam yang bekerja di pertanian di Jepang menyembunyikan kehamilannya karena takut dipulangkan. Bayi kembarnya lahir meninggal dan ia divonis menelantarkan jenazah. MA membebaskannya.
